newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Commerzbank to expand in Central Europe.
newsitem.headline: Commerzbank to expand in Central Europe.

text.p: Germany's Commerzbank AG set up a new subsidiary in Budapest as part of its plans to strengthen its investment banking activity in Central eastern Europe, Hans-Ascan Wieck, managing director of the new uni told a news conference on Wednesday.
Wieck said Commerzbank already has a commercial bank unit in Hungary, an export finance bank in Poland, and two brokerages in the Czech Republic, one specialised in equity, the other in bond trading.
"But Commerzbank has decided to set up investment banks also in the region," he added.
Officials of the new unit, Eurocorpcommerz International Finance Rt said the company had a registered capital of 50 million forints, and was 51 percent owned by Commerzbank AG.

The remaining shares are held by Wolfgang Sietz, owner of the consultant company Eurocorp, which will finish its operations but part of its staff and business contacts, including a contract with Germany's RWE group, has been taken over by Eurocorpcommerz.

RWE acquired substantial stakes in two of Hungary's electricity distribution companies and the Matra power station and plans to invest billions of German marks for developments in Hungary, Sietz said.
Eurocorpcommerz officials said that Commerzbank AG, through its new subsidiary, may take part in ensuring financing for these developments.
